findings.text: non-blocking: _MOVE_SOURCE_BINDING_CYPHER writes a second copy of the drained test and of the supersede-plus-receipt update instead of embedding supersede_drained_name_cypher, so the 'one builder' the run's own docstring and evidence fragment claim does not cover the compose/attach move; the copy already differs (origin hardcoded 'compose', run_id null) and can drift from source_invariant.py:61.

non-blocking: _supersede_update creates the StandardNameChange receipt itself with randomUUID() and a literal operation interpolated into the query text, duplicating record_standard_name_change (provenance_lifecycle.py:1981), which already accepts a transaction query handle and is the receipt writer the other supersession paths use; the repository now has a fourth receipt shape for one lifecycle event.

non-blocking: _supersede_released_bindings and the released_out plumbing added to _lock_claimed_name_bindings have no test at all; test_last_source_supersede.py drives retarget, recovery and mark_sources_composed only, so a regression in both claimed-attachment writers or in mark_sources_attached would redden nothing while the suite stays green.

non-blocking: in stage_claimed_generated_candidates the supersession names the staged candidate as successor without ever writing its PRODUCED_NAME edge in that transaction, unlike persist_claimed_attachments (line 1465) which MERGEs the binding first; a rich write that then fails leaves the former holder superseded pointing at a candidate that produces nothing.

non-blocking: the [refine] parametrisation only changes the operation label on the same retarget_standard_name_sources call, so it re-runs the retarget case under a different name and never enters persist_refined_name; the coverage it appears to add to the refine writer is the retarget primitive, already covered by the [retarget] case.
